plan_notes: RECENCY: lead with outlet RSS / sitemap_news.xml feeds (rss_feeds_first) and filter by pubDate within the 72h window (since 2026-10-14T22:00Z). WebSearch site: queries tend to return evergreen pages - use WebSearch only to fill gaps, and verify every published time on the article page itself. Note 10-18 is a Sunday (KST): Friday-Saturday US/EU releases are the freshest primary documents.
OUTPUT: write candidates under the key "items" (NOT "candidates").

SCOPE: follow sources.json categories[politics]._note - three axes only: (1) policy/regulation, (2) AI in elections & public opinion, (3) AI geopolitics. No AI-less general politics; if deleting AI from the headline leaves a standing story, drop it. Aim for spread across all three axes and regions (US federal/state, EU, UK, Korea, China/Asia, LatAm).

BALANCE: 10-17 shipped 5 policy/geopolitics cards (CMA, EU RAISE, AI Act pressure, Brookings, China open-weight) and zero elections-axis cards - prioritize elections/public-opinion (deepfakes, provenance, influence ops, Brazil TSE) and hard geopolitics decisions (BIS rules, smuggling indictments, datacenter siting) today.

NEUTRALITY: non-partisan; report what was decided/filed/published; attribute contested claims to the named party; no horse-race or polling commentary (esp. Brazil runoff, US midterms). Prefer primary documents; primary doc and news report about it are ONE story.

DEDUP: do not resubmit anything in recently_published_do_not_resubmit. Follow-ups qualify only with a NEW ruling, filing, bill, executive order or official release (e.g. EO 14409 framework text, SIF rule text, TSE ruling on Meta AI, formal EU AI Office decision, Korea AI Basic Act amendment National Assembly passage, CMA final SMS decision). Commentary/analysis/reactions on published events are dropped.
Paywalled/crawler-blocked majors (reuters, bloomberg, ft, wsj, nytimes, economist, foreignpolicy) are excluded - find the same decision on an allowed outlet or the primary source.
